title: Triage an unknown binary statically before opening a heavy tool
summary: Order for facing an unknown artifact: file, ELF header, dependencies, then strings as xref anchors before any decompiler; empty strings is not proof of packing.

title: Read ELF headers before choosing architecture, tool, or address model
summary: Settle class, endianness, machine, type and entry from readelf before debugging, so PIE base, address model and disassembler settings are decided by evidence.

title: Pick the analysis tool family from real content type, not the file extension
summary: Magic bytes decide the branch: compiled code to a disassembler, OLE/OOXML containers to oletools, scripts read directly; extensions lie on purpose.

title: Pivot from one distinctive string to the security-relevant function
summary: Locate a distinctive literal, show its references, walk to callers until you reach external input or an authorization decision; zero references is a real result.

title: Judge decompiler output instead of believing it
summary: Treat pseudocode as a hypothesis: confirm the comparison in the listing, rename only proven values, and test in a fixture before building an exploit or patch.

title: Separate library code from program logic before reading a function
summary: Rank imports by consequence (exec, file, network) and start from their callers; static binaries need string-signature separation instead, and library code is not the challenge.

title: Inspect exactly the memory you need with GDB's x command
summary: Choose count, format and unit deliberately, dump before and after the step under test, and keep dumps bounded; a pointer and its target are different dumps.

title: Prove parser behavior with a before/after memory snapshot, not with inference
summary: Two identical-input snapshots around one call plus one prediction that changes exactly one field; identical dumps or unpredicted layouts mean the model is wrong.

title: Triage Office macros with olevba before reading any VBA
summary: One analysis run tells you whether macros exist and what is flagged; read only implicated modules in entry-point order, and treat 'no macro' as inconclusive.

title: Rank macro indicators by consequence instead of reading VBA top to bottom
summary: Bucket indicators as execution, network, persistence, file/registry, obfuscation and work them in order; the challenge prompt breaks ties, and decoys are common.

title: Extract embedded OLE objects and keep their provenance
summary: Extract into a dedicated directory, hash and label parentage immediately, classify by content, and record 'nothing extracted' as a real negative result.

title: Reverse a service binary when no source is provided
summary: Capture deterministic legitimate behavior first and use it as the regression test, then reverse only the input path the checker exercises; one owner per service.

title: Classify an opaque value before attempting to decode it
summary: Decide by usage: equality-compared and stable means identifier or digest, strict-decodable means encoding, one-time with a tag means keyed; then route to the right card.

title: Decode hex only when its structure supports the claim
summary: Check alphabet and parity, decode once, inspect magic and structure; explain odd lengths instead of padding them, and never decode a digest you cannot attack.

title: Use strict Base64 decoding so failures mean something
summary: Decode with validate=True, treat an error as information, admit URL-safe only with a second reason, and let decoded structure - not exit status - be the evidence.

title: Stop recursive decoding when a layer stops adding structure
summary: Predict each layer's evidence before running it, log the layers, and switch strategy after two structure-free layers; a named mechanism in the prompt skips the search.

title: Treat CyberChef Magic as a hypothesis list, never as an answer
summary: Run a pinned local build shallow, verify the top candidate with an independent strict decoder, and discard candidates that only explain the crib; no hit is a result.

title: Derive an XOR key from a known plaintext prefix, then test it beyond the crib
summary: Normalize to bytes, XOR the crib, read the key pattern to pick single-byte versus repeating versus keystream, and require coherence beyond the crib.

title: Rank all 256 single-byte XOR keys instead of guessing them
summary: Score all 256 keys locally with printable-plus-language terms, accept only whole-string coherence, and stop rather than escalating when no candidate is coherent.

title: Cancel XOR terms algebraically before attacking any key
summary: Write the equations and cancel the shared keystream to turn key recovery into a plaintext-difference problem; alignment errors and additive ciphers are the traps.

title: Predict service credentials from a weakly seeded PRNG
summary: Trace generator and seed, reproduce issued values locally before predicting anything, then replace only the generation call with a secure source - seeding changes are not a fix.

title: Treat an exposed PRNG state as disclosure of future service secrets
summary: Confirm exposure with a prediction against your own instance, map which generator feeds the security value, then remove exposure and change that value's entropy source only.

title: Model a hash-shaped identifier's input space before enumerating it
summary: Entropy comes from inputs, not digest length; reproduce a known identifier locally before planning bounded enumeration, and patch by adding randomness plus ownership checks.

title: Decide against brute force before you start it
summary: Write space size, measured per-attempt cost and budget; if any is unknown do not start, and if the target is live check automation rules before a single request.

title: Split a physical or hardware puzzle into device, transport, and service layers
summary: Prove device, transport and service layers separately, reset the device between tests, serialize who touches hardware, and log which layer each failure belonged to.

title: Treat a non-standard HID report descriptor as the protocol specification
summary: Decode the report descriptor first and build the decoder from report IDs, widths, counts and ranges; swapping layouts or encodings never fixes wrong report framing.

title: Reconstruct an unusual protocol when no dissector understands it
summary: Follow the raw stream, propose framing, and require the model to partition the whole stream; undecoded traffic is not evidence of encryption, and truncation explains many cases.

title: Suspect environment parity before rewriting a failing exploit
summary: Compare capabilities, processes and listeners between container and full system; reproduce where the capability exists, and never disable environment components to make a local test pass.

title: Find the real owner of a port before blaming the service
summary: Use ss to identify the listener's owner, classify it as your leftover process, your supervisor's, or the environment's, and fix your own configuration rather than other components.

title: Bank partial credit from artifacts before you understand the challenge
summary: Extract cost-ordered artifacts, type and hash each with provenance, route them to specialists, and claim whatever they yield before investing in full challenge comprehension.

title: Handle the hidden encoding layer after an artifact decode
summary: Use alphabet and length to admit one or two candidate encodings, validate structure, and treat an alphabet off the standard table as a substitution rather than another encoder attempt.

title: Make the automation challenge correct once before making it parallel
summary: Solve one sample, prove generalization on a second, add structured output, then parallelize with bounds and a kill switch; external automation stays dry-run until rules are known.
